paragraphs: Rava ben Ha-Madori. First chapter of Yevamot; Shmuel's pupil. He erred, thinking that Rava was Ha-Madori's son, and departed from the plain meaning: Rava said that Ha-Madori's son explained it to him. So too Shabbat 107, end of b, 125, beginning of a: ‘Rava said: bar Ha-Madori explained it to me.’ Rashi explains: Ha-Madori's son explained the matter's reasoning to me (see above, ben Ha-Madori). Similarly Rava said: ‘Bar Ahina explained it to me’; ‘Adda Mari explained it to me’; ‘Adda the surveyor explained it to me’; ‘Idi explained it to me’; ‘Ravin bar Rav Sheva explained it to me.’
